items.title: A morphism from a reduced scheme into a set of mutually incomparable points of a locally Noetherian scheme factors through that discrete set
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a morphism from a reduced scheme into a set of points of a locally Noetherian scheme with no nontrivial specializations among them factors through the disjoint union of those points (statement lines 15616-15622). The counted proof is short and complete: the singleton case is cited, the finite case follows because the induced topology on the set is discrete so the source splits into its fibres, and the general case is reduced to the finite one over an affine chart by replacing the given set with the finite set of minimal primes of the image subring, which is contained in the image because of the minimal prime statement and exhausts the image because everything else is a specialization (proof lines 15624-15643). It is H2: all three reductions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard statements about points and minimal primes.
